focus: Angle 10: Failure modes. Inspect over/under-triggering, command-skill ambiguity, child recursion, loop stops and prompt-budget loss.
noveltyJustification: Three findings add one-sided prompt-gate coverage, explicit leaf-recursion controls and conflicting stop-policy configuration; two extend prior ambiguity and brief-budget evidence.
keyQuestions: Which one canonical inventory reconciles command metadata, active bridge allow-list rows and doctor routing declarations for all 45 slash commands?
How should command intent and skill intent combine so plain planning and research prompts reach the matching workflow with acceptable recall and precision?
What should a command recommendation show, and which commands can the model invoke directly versus asking first?
How does a plain chat request reach the appropriate command workflow across supported runtimes, and how should skills link to command front doors?
What benchmark evidence, prior art and failure controls should validate the design?
ruledOut: Using prompt fire/no-fire coverage that checks only positive routeable examples as the sole overtrigger regression gate.
Treating confidence alone as execution authority.
Allowing a leaf executor to re-enter a parent loop or launch the same CLI from itself.
Treating the 80-token cap as a guarantee that the full rendered brief, including directives, remains within that token estimate.

label: The prompt-policy replay fails on undertrigger when a positive gold row is declined, but does not assert that gold-none prompts abstain; the corpus scorer separately counts false fires on none. The replay is therefore not an overtrigger guard by itself.

Typed slash evidence holds the named command above a related dependency and suppresses false ambiguity, while the same words without slash syntax remain ambiguous. Keep ambiguity and action policy explicit: a high skill match alone does not resolve whether the command runs or asks under Gate 3.

The deep-research command YAML owns the loop and dispatches a one-iteration leaf; the mode contract forbids nested CLI loops and the leaf definition denies Task/sub-agent dispatch. A child that re-enters the parent workflow can multiply work or recurse, so command routing should carry execution depth and leaf boundaries with the workflow.

The lineage config sets maxIterations 10 and top-level stopPolicy max-iterations, but nested antiConvergence.stopPolicy says fail-closed; the workflow treats the iteration cap as the first terminal check. Keep one authoritative stop-policy value or test precedence, because conflicting stop fields can otherwise change whether convergence continues to the cap.

The default brief cap is 80 tokens and the ambiguous branch requires a cap above 80; a command companion is omitted when it does not fit, while the directives and hygiene suffix are appended after the capped portion. Tests confirm both the companion-drop case and the fit case, so required command/action fields should not live only in an optional companion line.
